title: Crypto misuse: CBC key bytes stored as plaintext copy in ctx
description: wolfssl_aes_cbc_ctx stores a plaintext copy of the raw key bytes in key_bytes[32] alongside the wolfCrypt Aes struct which also holds the expanded key schedule. This creates two copies of the key in memory: the wolfCrypt key schedule (zeroized by wc_AesFree) and the raw key bytes (zeroized by memzero_explicit in sess_free). The raw copy exists for sess_reset, which re-calls wc_AesSetKey. Consequence: if a memory disclosure occurs between sess_init and sess_free, the raw AES key is directly readable as a contiguous 32-byte field at a known offset within wolfssl_aes_cbc_ctx. The wolfCrypt Aes struct's key schedule is less directly readable. GCM does NOT store a plaintext key copy (no reset re-keying needed). CBC is inconsistent with GCM and stores unnecessary additional key material exposure. Trigger: any memory disclosure (e.g. kernel heap spray, side channel) during an active CBC session window. Crypto consequence: raw AES key bytes readable in addition to the expanded key schedule.
